messages:
Maya: quick sync — we've been hitting a tension between staging-queue sampling depth and intake latency for new models. propose: keep admit path fast, but dispatch an async gating pipeline that pulls ~2% of live traffic for full bench + ensure every model gets a deterministic golden-run within the first 10 minutes. thoughts? @Omar @Priya

Omar: so two lanes: fast admit (happy path) + async full validation. Clarify what 2% means — 2% of overall requests or 2% of probe requests per-model?

Priya: async makes sense. 2% overall will kill costs for embeddings-heavy workloads. Suggest sample rate proportional to model's tokens-per-request with a hard token budget cap. Also: golden-run should land on warm nodes to avoid cold-start skew.

Ken: big caveat — async is only safe if we have fallback policies when validations fail. otherwise regressions slip through. Proposal: admit_status ∈ {accepted, pending_validations, blocked}. API returns accepted+pending but includes a 'quality_risk' header.

Maya: agree. For hard failures (>=3 failures on golden set) auto-rollback. For soft regressions, emit alerts and block promotion to Dedicated pools.

Omar: sampling should be stratified across traffic slices (prompt length buckets, batch shapes, quantization mode). uniform sampling misses edge cases.

Priya: also important — metrics collected in async bench must match runtime paths: kv cache warm, batching shapes, prefix cache. Capture a minimal runtime trace and replay in bench harness.

Ken: interface thought — decouple admit RPC from promote RPC. Admit returns model_id + admit_token. Promote requires validation_artifact. Keeps infra surface area small.

Maya: pseudo-config for sampling:

```
staging_sampling:
  mode: stratified
  strata: [short, med, long]
  rate_per_stratum: [0.05, 0.02, 0.01]
  golden_run:
    every_model: true
    window_s: 600
  token_budget_per_hour: 1e7
  anneal_on_traffic: true
```

Priya: tiny tweak: add anneal_on_traffic (good call). Also include per-model cap so one noisy model can't burn whole budget.

Omar: ops Q — where does dispatch run? central runner or per-region workers? prefer per-region for locality, but need a global coordinator to ensure golden uniqueness.

Ken: lightweight global ledger (model_id -> golden_done_at) + per-region dispatchers that consult it. eventual consistency is ok.

Maya: long-term: unify probe scheduling with canary sequencer. We have two schedulers now; merging reduces duplication and gives consistent rollout semantics. But do it carefully.

Priya: +1 for consolidation but don't blow up sequencer SLA. Maybe extract a shared scheduler library first.

Omar: implementation steps I foresee:
1) API change: admit + admit_token flow (backwards compatible)
2) staging sampling service: per-region dispatcher + global ledger
3) bench harness adapters to run with runtime traces
4) rollout: feature-flag per-customer default (opt-out for small customers)

Ken: monitoring contract suggestions: validation_latency_p50,p95,p99; regression_count; golden_false_positive_rate; budget_burn_rate. Also expose admit_status metrics.

Maya: action items: @Omar spec ledger API; @Priya draft bench-harness runtime-trace shim; @Ken write admit/promotion API proto. I'll draft rollout matrix + cost estimate this week.

deploy-bot: Maya pinned a message: "staging sampling RFC follow-up" — review in 3 business days.

Priya: I'll add a small perf sim to the RFC to show token-cost tradeoffs.

Omar: will mock ledger protobuf + post demo script for per-region dispatch tomorrow.

Ken: adding quality_risk header schema to API proposal.

Maya: request: keep initial sampling conservative until bench-repro is rock-solid. We'll widen after controlled ramp.

Priya: :thumbsup:

Omar: ack

Ken: ack

Maya: closing thread, will open RFC link shortly.
